draft_evidence.quote:
A cord with a stake at one end does, and a wheel does, and a bowl does, and every one of those is a thing somebody made. That's still geometry.

Nobody dressed that floor. Nobody laid it. It was made some other way, and I don't have a word for the way, and I'm not going to invent one.

comparison_evidence.quote:
NOTHING beyond the three facts; no maker, no purpose, no 'Architect'.

No maker, purpose, intelligence, 'Architect', 'primordial', 'before the system' in anyone's mouth or narration; Karis states three facts and refuses a verb; [UNBOUND] appears once only.

findings.consequence: The packet approves 'Somebody made a floor' only inside the fixed final three-facts speech and requires no maker or theory beyond it. These earlier statements both posit somebody and infer an unknown manufacture method, giving the reader the prohibited interpretive step before Karis's staged refusal to connect the facts.
findings.repair_target: Keep the early geometry and surface observations at the level of shape, tool marks, joins, and measurable weathering; reserve the only maker wording for the fixed closing speech and do not infer an alternate manufacture method.

draft_evidence.quote:
The academy above Ostrand. Built, not converted; every course laid under the registry's own standard, the mortar mixed to its own directive. Fifty years, near enough, and I can show you the tool that dressed it, because the tool's still in use.

A records hall's back wall, in Ardenmere. Two hundred years, near enough. Same era as the papers in a case Seln carries and hasn't opened, and I can put the mortar against the paper's watermark and get the same generation.

Greyvane's old course, the one under the converted waystation's floor — older than the academy by a good deal, laid by people who dressed stone with a wider chisel than anyone's used since.

Waystation stone, from the wall Prynn's archive sat inside. Four hundred years, by the archive's own ledger, which I read the entry in. It's the oldest dressed stone I have ever had in my hand and it is the floor of my ruler.

comparison_evidence.quote:
she dates the fused stone against every masonry stratum in her three boxes (registry-era, standardization-era, pre-standardization, founding-era waystation stone from Prynn's archive)

Any new named entity; any stratum or dating fact beyond those listed; any additional [UNBOUND] use.

findings.consequence: The packet authorizes the four strata and their required ordering, but explicitly reserves any additional stratum or dating fact for approval. The manuscript adds specific buildings, construction histories, ages, tool continuity, chisel chronology, mortar/watermark equivalence, and an 'oldest dressed stone in Valdris' superlative with no recorded exception. Those claims silently become reusable canon if the chapter advances.
findings.repair_target: Limit the on-page comparison to the packet-listed strata and already approved Book 6 facts, or obtain explicit approval for each added provenance/dating claim before advancement.

draft_evidence.quote: She worked with her voice for the first time since the ring. It had come back, as Oryn said it would, in pieces, over days, and by the week's middle it was a low usable thing that went on her when she pushed it and came back when she rested it, and she rested it by writing.

comparison_evidence.quote:
Karis documented all of it, because that was her seat, and she did it on the afternoon of the third day in the loft, with the three boxes open round her and her voice back.

Karis and Brom argued for a quarter of an hour, hoarse against deep, about whether an apple baked with honey in it was a thing the hold had *made* or a thing it had *had*, and Karis lost on the merits and said so.

findings.consequence: Chapter 15 opens the day after Chapter 14, where Karis already documents aloud and sustains a quarter-hour argument. Calling the new week her first voice work since the Ring resets a recovery beat the reader just witnessed and makes the injury chronology visibly inconsistent.
findings.repair_target: Carry forward the already usable, hoarse voice and describe how Karis budgets or further recovers it during the report without calling this its first post-Ring use.

draft_evidence.quote: Wind. Iron Skin. Ember. Shadow. Tide. Iron rank one, Copper, no ranking, Bronze, Iron rank four. Five people, five Paths, five tiers, five histories of a thing that showed up at fourteen and has been each of ours since.

comparison_evidence.quote: every Arbiter in the party went silent at the same line, same stride, same instant, same way — Wind, Iron Skin, Ember, Shadow, Tide, Iron R1 to Bronze

findings.consequence: The list contains five people and five Paths, but only three named tiers—Iron, Copper, Bronze—with Iron repeated and Karis holding no ranking. The phrase 'five tiers' is an audible arithmetic error inside a passage whose persuasive force depends on exact classification.
findings.repair_target: Describe the five formal standings without claiming they are five distinct tiers.

draft_evidence.quote:
The rubbings first, because they were the largest: eleven sheets, one per upright, charcoal on the registry's own paper turned to its blank side, each sheet the height of the stone it had been taken from and cut to that height, so that the eleven lay on the table in the order the uprights stood and at their own sizes, tallest to shortest, a ring laid flat.

Every band is the same kind of line and never the same line, and I want to know how many kinds there are before I say anything about any of them.

comparison_evidence.quote: The copied carvings as objects (lines in no alphabet she owns), the paced perimeter's arithmetic recalled, the stake's number.

findings.consequence: The carvings are strongly realized as physical rubbings and a private tally, but a full-draft search for 'alphabet' returns zero and no equivalent statement says they are outside every alphabet Karis owns. The chapter therefore omits one explicit property of the required Ch10 payoff and risks recoding unreadable writing as merely a taxonomy of line forms.
findings.repair_target: State in Karis's evidence register that the copied lines belong to no alphabet she owns, without interpreting or naming them.

strengths: Yes: worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. Paper purchases access to the room, grain changes where the party sleeps, a healer's route becomes an audible backlog, research is physical comparison and filing discipline, and institutional concealment is embodied by numbered iron, map blanks, and registry prose.

There is no fight or combat set piece, exactly as prohibited, so the terrain and 'X removed Y's ability to Z' combat tests are not applicable. The research sequence is nevertheless a memorable procedural set piece: the table and samples are load-bearing, and Karis's bounded win is writable as 'Karis removed inference's ability to pass as evidence by stopping her pen before the verb.'

The five-finding architecture is lucid and cumulative. Each movement changes the kind of evidence—grammar, simultaneous failure, physical age, institutional record, then interpretation—and the repeated acts of laying out, writing, turning, and stopping give Karis a distinct professional action vocabulary.

Karis's fifth finding is especially strong character work. Holding the nib above the page makes methodological honesty physical, 'It's a fear' gives the refusal emotional cost, and Lira's 'Does it help?' / 'It's just correct' exchange preserves both voices without declaring affection.

Cael remains active in a chapter centered on someone else's competence: he learns Karis's reach order, supplies the slip, recognizes the difference between her rule and his debt, and converts that recognition into 'Lira first. Tomorrow.'

The fixed ending lands cleanly. The mid-scene log turns Chapter 16 into an obligation, the log is closed before the final speech, and the last dialogue differs from Chapter 14's log ending without an explanatory tail.

Production hygiene is strong: 4,843 words falls within tolerance; metadata, summary-substitution, modern-register, feeling/growth, pitch, and chapter-level anti-tic searches are clean; attribution survives all multi-speaker scenes; names pass the registry ear check; and [UNBOUND] appears exactly once.
concerns: Taste only: the substituted loom-and-sluice image is vivid, audible, and more rooted in the hold's material world than 'equipment on a circuit.' The packet repeatedly specifies the equipment/circuit formulation but does not label that sentence verbatim as it does 'It's a fear' and the closing exchange; a human may want to decide whether preserving the exact cross-book plant outweighs the stronger in-world image.

Taste only: the strata movement is deliberately expansive and tactile, but its successive tool, mortar, paper, chisel, weathering, and ruler explanations make the third finding much longer than the other four. After the approval-required factual additions are resolved, a line pass could test whether every comparison is needed for the reader to accept the limit.

Taste only: 'the woman had said something ... and after that nobody touched a sheet' creates a pleasantly implied authority beat, but the unsaid sentence is unusually coy inside an otherwise exact chapter. It works as scale and social texture rather than a contract defect.
